newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce's Daley sees solid growth but no boom.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce's Daley sees solid growth but no boom.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of Commerce William Daley said Friday he sees the U.S. economy continuing on a solid growth path but not at the boom pace of last year and early this year.
"We won't have the sort of growth we had last year, but we will have good solid growth that is based upon solid foundations," Daley said in an interview with Reuters.
"I think it is going to continue, not the boom attitude, but just the solidness of this ecoomy because it is based on some pretty good foundations," he added.
Daley said he sees some further boost to the economy and public attitudes from the balanced budget pact once the details are worked out and it is put into law.
"That is going to be a big boost not only for people's confidence, but also their business plans," he said. "I don't think that has been factored in a lot."

He said he does not believe the U.S. business community is "giddy" about the current health of the U.S. economy, but said that when he talks with business leaders he does not get a sense that they see a lot of clouds on the horizon.

The U.S. economy grew by a robust 5.8 percent annual rate during the first three months of the year, following a healthy 3.8 percent rate of growth during the last three months of 1996. But many economists believe the economy will slow significantly during the current quarter as consumers pull back on spending.

Daley said inflation remains under control. The U.S. Labor Department reported on Friday that producer prices fell for the fifth straight month in a row, dropping by 0.3 percent in May. It was the first time in 45 years that wholesale prices have dropped for five consecutive months.
